chapter: Chicago and Oliver's band in California
title: The Oliver band in San Francisco and Minor Hall's firing
summary: Playing at a dance hall on Walker Street in San Francisco with Oliver; lineup and Oliver firing drummer Minor Hall and violinist Jimmy Palao without notice.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh yeah. See, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that was over in Frisco and I was playing over to the Picola Dance Hall on Walker Street.
Who was the drummer with you there with all of them?
Oh, we started out with Minor Hall, Ram.

They fired Jimmy Polar. Oh yeah. I remember that. You see, I'll give you the lineup of the band we left fairly well with. We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums. Okay. Then, they want to turn this boy loose, give him a note. Didn't give him no notice. Just fired him.

You know what I have to say? You bring this man to the end of the Southern Pacific line. They want to fire him. They want to send him back. He said, well, come me out too. We had David Jones with us too. He played mellophone and sax.
